5.1. Dataset Design                                                  In VL-MIA, the model’s training data is private, making
                                                                     membership labels uncertain so that large distribution bias
The proposed OpenLVLM-MIA benchmark dataset enables
                                                                     is introduced by mixing temporally mismatched data and
independent evaluation of membership across the entire
                                                                     DALL-E–generated images. In contrast, OpenLVLM-MIA
training pipeline, i.e., vision encoder pretraining, projector
                                                                     adopts models trained on public data; thus, membership can
pretraining, and instruction tuning, because LVLM training
                                                                     be verified. By selecting data from the same period and
typically proceeds in multiple stages, each relying on a dif-
                                                                     domain, distribution bias is minimized. Moreover, while
ferent dataset. The key features are as follows:
                                                                     VL-MIA evaluates only the final model, OpenLVLM-MIA
• High transparency: All training data are public, guaran-           evaluates all three stages independently, enabling analy-
   teeing membership ground truth.                                   sis of where and how membership information is retained.
• Three-stage evaluation: It covers vision encoder pre-              These improvements enable fair assessment of whether
   training, projector pretraining, and instruction tuning.          MIA methods detect membership rather than distribution
• Scale: It consists of 1,000 member and 1,000 non-                  bias.
   member images per stage (6,000 total).

sures distance between distributions in the Reproducing               it difficult to visualize separation in 3D space using un-
kernel Hilbert space. We use the RBF kernel k(x, y) =                 supervised methods. Therefore, in this study, we quanti-
exp(−γ∥x − y∥2 ) and set the kernel width γ −1 by the me-             fied separability using supervised dimensionality reduction
dian heuristic (the median of all pairwise distances). Signif-        with membership labels, where the Fisher discriminant axis

erative models. In this study, we use it to measure distances         criminant axis. This makes any separation (or its absence)

This work focuses only on LLaVA-1.5 (7B). We did not
